sources.entry: Mere Medical ⚠ - Manage all of your medical records from Epic MyChart, Cerner, and OnPatient patient portals in one place. Privacy-focused, self-hosted, and offline-first. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Mere Medical is a self-hosted, offline-first web app that aggregates and syncs medical records from multiple patient portals into one timeline.
summary.what_it_does: Mere Medical pulls medical records from patient portals and electronic medical record systems into a single personal health record. The README says it supports thousands of hospitals and clinics and major EMR systems, naming Epic MyChart, Cerner, OnPatient, Veradigm, VA, Healow, Athena Health and NextGen. Records can be viewed in a timeline or summarized. It is described as self-hosted and offline-first, with core functionality meant to work without internet access. Portal access depends on per-provider client IDs and secrets set as environment variables. The app is deployed with Docker Compose or built locally with Nx, Node.js and npm.
use_cases: aggregate medical records from multiple patient portals
view health records in a timeline
sync Epic MyChart records to your own server
keep medical data private and offline-first
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml with the cfu288/mere-medical image, port 4200:8080, and the required client ID environment variables, including PUBLIC_URL.
Run docker compose up to start the app on port 4200.
For local development: git clone the repo, then run nvm install v26.7.0, nvm use, and npm install.
Install Nx globally with npm i nx -g, then run npx nx migrate --run-migrations if prompted.
Copy apps/api/.example.env to apps/api/.env and edit apps/web/src/environments/config.json with your values.
Run npx nx run-many --target=serve --projects=api,web --output-style=stream to start the full app.
stack: Angular (web app, inferred from the web/e2e project names)
notable: Connects to many EMR and patient portal providers, each with its own client ID setup
Offline-first design goal: core functions should work without internet
Documented design goals prioritize user control, privacy, and local-first storage
Supports both legacy DSTU2 and newer R4 FHIR endpoints for Epic and Cerner
Single-developer project maintained alongside a medical residency
caveats: Some providers need separate developer credentials; the VA client ID only works with the VA sandbox, not production
The README says the project is still labeled pre-release, though the maintainer notes it has been stable since 2022
Supported by a single developer with limited time; hosting costs are noted as a concern
keywords: view all my health data in one place
